title: The persisting influence of organized sports participation on mental health and wellness: a longitudinal repeated measures study of adolescent female athletes.
authors: Meyers R, Brna ML, Hogg-Cornejo V, Donahue C, Sweeney EA, Armento A, Howell DR.
figures: Box plots describing the self-reported ratings for  (A)  anxiety,  (B)  depressive symptoms,  (C)  grit,  (D)  peer relationships,  (E)  fatigue, and  (F)  body appreciation at the post-season and 6-month post-season follow-up time points.

Comparison between adolescent female athletes who did and did not report active organized sport at the 6-month post-season assessment on ratings of  (A)  anxiety,  (B)  depressive symptoms,  (C)  grit,  (D)  peer relationships,  (E)  fatigue, and  (F)  body appreciation.
tables: Descriptive characteristics of the participants who enrolled in the study and completed the post-season and 6-month follow up evaluations ( N  = 59).

Results from each multivariable regression model evaluating the effect of group (predictor: did and did not continue to participate in sports at the 6-month follow-up assessment) and each outcome measures (anxiety ratings, depressive symptoms, grit, peer relationships, or fatigue, and body appreciation ratings adjusting for covariates (post-season rating, physical activity level, age, and BMI).
